title_en: Guiding Case No. 226: Chen, Liu — intentional injury and maltreatment
ruling_gist_en: 1. A minor who is in a relatively stable cohabitation relationship with an unmarried partner of his or her parent(s) shall be recognized as a "family member" as defined in Article 260 of the Criminal Law. 2. In the course of habitual abuse, if the perpetrator commits severe violence against the victim, subjectively intends or is indifferent to causing injury, and objectively causes the victim to suffer minor injury or above, this shall be found to constitute the crime of intentional injury; if, after independent evaluation of the injury conduct, the other abusive acts still meet the elements of the crime of maltreatment, the perpetrator shall be punished for both the crime of intentional injury and the crime of maltreatment with cumulative sentencing. 3. In cases of intentional injury to minors, when determining whether the conduct constitutes "causing serious disability" by especially cruel means resulting in serious injury as provided in paragraph 2 of Article 234 of the Criminal Law, a comprehensive assessment shall be made taking into account factors such as the degree and number of disabilities, the body parts involved, and the serious impact of the injury on the minor's developing physical and mental health, and a correct judgment shall be made in accordance with the law.

full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. 226

Chen, Liu — case of intentional injury and maltreatment

(Discussed and adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, promulgated on May 30, 2024)

Keywords

Criminal / intentional injury; maltreatment; minor; family member; causing serious injury by extremely cruel means resulting in severe disability

Ruling Gist

1. A minor who is in a relatively stable state of cohabitation with an unmarried cohabiting partner of a parent shall be deemed a "family member" as provided in Article 260 of the Criminal Law.

2. Where, in the course of frequent maltreatment, the perpetrator commits serious violence against the victim, subjectively intending to or being reckless as to causing, and objectively causing, injuries of minor injury or above, the act shall be convicted as intentional injury; if, after independently evaluating such injurious act, the remaining maltreatment conduct still meets the constitutive elements of the crime of maltreatment, the perpetrator shall be punished for both intentional injury and maltreatment under concurrent sentence.

3. For cases of intentional injury against minors, in determining whether the circumstances meet the requirement of "causing serious injury by extremely cruel means resulting in severe disability" under Article 234, paragraph 2, of the Criminal Law, comprehensive consideration shall be given to factors such as the degree and number of disabilities, the body parts involved, and the severe impact of the injury consequences on the developing physical and mental health of the minor, so as to make an accurate judgment in accordance with the law.

Basic Facts

The defendant Liu was the mother of the victim Tong (a pseudonym, female, born in March 2014). After Liu divorced, Tong was directly raised by Liu. In November 2019, Liu met the defendant Chen and later began a romantic relationship and cohabited with him.

On February 13, 2020, the defendant Chen became displeased because Tong was video-chatting with her father, and thus slapped, kicked, and otherwise assaulted Tong. As a result, Liu took Tong away from Chen’s residence and proposed breaking up with Chen. On the evening of February 17, Chen came to Liu’s residence, and, angry over the breakup, immediately kicked Tong to the ground upon entering, then violently kicked Tong several times on the head, body, and legs. The next day, Liu took Tong to seek medical treatment. Tong was diagnosed with forehead contusion and chin laceration. Thereafter, to avoid Chen, Liu took Tong to stay temporarily at a friend's home. During this period, Chen repeatedly apologized to Liu and asked for forgiveness. On March 20 of the same year, Liu resumed her relationship with Chen and moved with Tong into Chen’s residence.

After that, during their cohabitation, the defendant Chen frequently, for no reason or under various pretexts such as disciplining the child, injured Tong by means such as punching and kicking, beating with a washboard, and burning with cigarette butts, causing multiple injuries to Tong’s body. Chen also frequently subjected Tong to corporal punishment and maltreatment by forcing her to kneel on a washboard for extended periods, swallowing cigarette butts, exposure to cold and hunger, and humiliation. The defendant Liu, as Tong’s mother, failed to effectively stop Chen, allowed Chen to injure and maltreat Tong, and occasionally participated herself, causing Tong minor injuries.

In mid-May 2020, the defendant Chen was bathing Tong. When Tong complained that the water temperature was uncomfortable, Chen deliberately repeatedly adjusted the water temperature to the highest and lowest settings to scald Tong. When Liu heard Tong’s cries and entered the bathroom to check, Chen falsely claimed the water was not hot, so Liu closed the door and left. After the bath, Chen made Tong kneel as punishment. Liu noticed large blisters on Tong’s body from scalding but only applied burn ointment and did not promptly take her for medical treatment. It was not until late May that the two defendants took Tong to the hospital for treatment as the wounds were severely infected. Subsequently, upon another person’s report to the police, the two defendants were arrested.

Forensic examination determined that Tong’s burn and scald injuries reached Grade II severe injury (facial scald leaving superficial scar pigmentation changes, disability Grade VII), with five injuries classified as Grade I minor injury (including three disabilities at Grade IX) and five injuries as Grade II minor injury. It was also found that the victim Tong incurred medical expenses, nutritional fees, and other costs totaling RMB 202,767.35 during treatment.

After the case was filed, the people’s court lawfully revoked the guardianship of the victim Tong’s mother Liu, transferred custody from Liu to the victim’s father, arranged for regular psychological counseling for Tong by a psychologist, and coordinated solutions for her school enrollment and living difficulties.

Judgment

On October 13, 2021, the Xinfu District People’s Court of Fushun City, Liaoning Province, rendered a criminal附带 civil judgment: 1. The defendant Chen was convicted of intentional injury and sentenced to fifteen years’ imprisonment; convicted of maltreatment and sentenced to two years’ imprisonment; the combined sentence was fixed at sixteen years’ imprisonment. 2. The defendant Liu was convicted of intentional injury and sentenced to two years’ imprisonment; convicted of maltreatment and sentenced to one year and six months’ imprisonment; the combined sentence was fixed at three years’ imprisonment. 3. The defendant Chen was ordered to compensate the plaintiff in the collateral civil action, Tong, in the amount of RMB 202,767.35. After the judgment was pronounced, there was no appeal or protest, and the judgment became legally effective.

Reasoning

The defendant Chen cohabited with the victim’s mother Liu, and together with Liu and the victim Tong, they were in a relatively stable state of cohabitation, forming a de facto family relationship. During the period of cohabitation with Liu and Tong, Chen subjected Tong to long-term, frequent abuse and torment by means of beating, corporal punishment, exposure to cold and hunger, and humiliation, with vile circumstances, thus constituting the crime of maltreatment. The defendant Liu, as Tong’s mother, failed to take effective measures to stop or prevent Chen’s maltreatment, repeatedly allowed it, and occasionally participated, also constituting the crime of maltreatment.

In the course of frequent and continuous maltreatment, the defendant Chen repeatedly directly injured Tong’s body using violent means such as burning with cigarette butts, scalding with hot water, and punching and kicking, causing one instance of severe injury and ten instances of minor injury, among other serious consequences. The intentional injury conduct involved could not be fully assessed under the crime of maltreatment alone and should be punished as intentional injury. The defendant Liu, as Tong’s mother, repeatedly allowed Chen to injure Tong and occasionally participated, causing Tong minor injuries, also constituting the crime of intentional injury. In addition, the frequent and continuous maltreatment by the two defendants also constituted the crime of maltreatment. If the defendants’ criminal conduct was only punished as intentional injury, the maltreatment conduct could not be fully assessed; therefore, they should be punished for both intentional injury and maltreatment under concurrent sentence.

According to Article 234 of the Criminal Law, whoever causes serious injury by extremely cruel means resulting in severe disability shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years, life imprisonment, or death. For general intentional injury cases, a disability of Grade VI or above is usually considered "severe disability." In this case, the victim’s physical injuries were assessed as Grade VII disability, but the injuries to different parts of her body resulted in multiple disabilities (one Grade VII disability and three Grade IX disabilities), causing extremely severe damage to the minor’s physical and mental health. Based on this, to maximize the protection of the minor’s interests, after comprehensive assessment, the circumstances in this case were determined to constitute "causing serious injury by extremely cruel means resulting in severe disability," and the defendant Chen was sentenced to fifteen years’ imprisonment for intentional injury.

In the joint crime, the defendant Chen played a principal role and was the principal offender. The defendant Liu played a secondary role and was an accessory; after being brought to justice, she truthfully confessed the facts, sincerely repented, and admitted guilt and accepted punishment. Moreover, Liu did not directly participate in the act of scalding Tong with hot water, which caused Grade II severe injury (disability Grade VII). Taking into comprehensive consideration the motives, means, circumstances, consequences, social harm, subjective malignancy, and personal dangerousness of the two defendants, the court rendered the above judgment in accordance with the law.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 234, Article 260 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China
